rationale:
I shot the town at 1600x950 and 390x844 before planning it, and then measured the frames per row rather than trusting my eye. The town proper is dense and genuinely good. What the phone frame says is that it occupies 46% of the canvas: ~26% above the roofline is empty sky, and ~22% below it is the near roof ramping from mean luma 117 down to 20. I am NOT planning against either. The bottom band is #105's foreground ramp doing exactly what it was built to do — at the shipping size it reads as a window vignette, not a hole — and #104 and #109 both spent their bets down there already. That closes c163 with a reason and turns the frame measurement into c174 for a later pass.

The real finding is in the census, not the picture. passages, tileKinds and speciesKinds have never moved in 114 iterations, and when I went to look at why, tileKinds and speciesKinds turn out not to be arbitrary: they are 15 tile constants (WALL 0 through TUNNEL 10, plus four) and 11 SPECIES, both unchanged since commit 1. Every one of the 114 iterations, including #100's near block and #110's working roof, has been a recombination of the same fifteen materials and the same eleven plants. That is the frozen thing in this town, and rung 4b names it explicitly — 'a new kind of tile or species'. So b116 is a GLASSHOUSE on the allotments: the first thing in the town you can see through, one new grid constant and one new species that only sows under glass, wired into snowAt, wetF, windowLit, mistAt and the harvest cycle rather than inventing state beside them. It must take tileKinds 135->144 and speciesKinds 99->108 — exact numbers, because both are per-snapshot counts summed over the census ladder's nine cells, so the brief prices its own success band instead of hoping. It serves the longest-untouched domain (Cross street & allotments, 10 back), it is 75 minutes and high risk, and it is second in the queue because b115 is a fifteen-minute instrument fix that must land first.

b115 is #114's question handed back answered. summarize() folds only planting.bySpecies and drops planted, blooming, daisies, mossy, matureTrees, worn, harvested and produce, so mossy — added by #103 SO THE CENSUS COULD SEE THE MOSS — moved 265->358 at #114 while the gate printed 'planting: unchanged'. #114 called it the manager's call because it reshapes the baseline. I am calling it, and putting it first so that b116's re-pin captures the new fields in the same move rather than re-pinning twice.

b117 collects three cues that are one subject: the town names more than it admits to naming (the cursor keys on answersTouch, the sowable-cell test, so everything #113 opened up is findable only by accident), names less than it draws (24 pieces of roof furniture, the most pointable things on a phone, say nothing), and names things it has hidden (nearHidden is draw-side only, so a walker behind the sill still answers). b118 is c168's measured regression — the lawn and lane birds are at a presence mean of 0.06 because their cap counts #106's roof birds against them, a one-word predicate bug with the counting already done. b119 gives FAR_GATE a door, which is the one place in the town where a person walks in out of nothing.

Curation. The budget was over for the fifth consecutive open and I fixed it this pass rather than deferring: 50.8 -> 43.8 KB, the most headroom of the run. LAWS.md opened at 12288/12288 with ZERO bytes free — the note I left myself last pass — so I cut before promoting: the standalone 'slow world scalar' law is folded into the ceiling law (six working instances embody it), 'ask what else enters a shared block' is MERGED into the rate-of-zero law because both are the same claim (your feature runs at zero while the counter lies to you), and the framing law lost the near-block examples now that the near block is built. That paid for seven promotions, all merged into their subjects rather than stacked: #112's hard-coded-hour and #114's fall-through-predicate findings, #113's pointer-vs-naming probe rule, #114's same-code control floor and its cross-region CA mask, #112's price-the-composite and untouched-axis rules. 15 laws at exactly 12288 bytes. The three tail ledger entries went 10.3 -> 5.4 KB with full text appended to the archive and the promoted Law: lines cut. Inventory back to nouns, with one factual CORRECTION I only found because I nearly briefed against it: rain and snow DO fall and ARE drawn, and the inventory never said so — I was one grep away from commissioning weather the town has had since #21.

queue.brief: THIS IS THE BET. Take the swing — a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. In 114 iterations the town's material vocabulary has never changed: `tileKinds` (135) and `speciesKinds` (99) are the two census scalars that have never moved, and that is not an accident of measurement — there are 15 tile constants (`WALL 0` through `TUNNEL 10`, plus four) and 11 `SPECIES`, both unchanged since commit 1. #100's near block and #110's working roof were both built entirely out of them. Build the town's first GLASSHOUSE, on the allotments (`ALT_X0 78`, plots `ox 80..90 x oy 8..50`, `ALT_GATE 86.5`, the shed, `POND` at 90,49.5). It should be the first thing in the town you can see THROUGH: a new grid constant (`GLASS`) with its own ground and roof treatment, a low span you read the plot rows through, and ONE new `SPECIES` entry — a tender crop, `veg`, sown only inside, so it keeps ripening when `bloomCap()` drops on the open plots outside. Wire it into what exists rather than beside it: `snowAt` lies on it, `wetF` beads on it, `windowLit`/`LIT_PANES` light it on a winter evening, `mistAt` hazes it, and `spawnAllotAgent`/`sendToPlot`/`ripePlots` treat its rows as plots so the block's own people work it. Why now: the allotments are the longest-untouched domain (10 back), and every other rung-4b this run has changed the map's extent — this one changes what the map is made OF, which is the axis nobody has moved.
queue.successLooksLike: The census reads `tileKinds` 135 -> 144 and `speciesKinds` 99 -> 108 — both are per-snapshot counts summed over the ladder's 9 cells, so those are the exact expected numbers, not a hope — and the baseline is re-pinned with `--save-baseline`. At 1600x950 midday the allotment block visibly contains a building it did not have, graded by a difference image quoted as a ratio to a same-code control run. On a January evening the glass is lit and something is still growing under it when the open plots are bare.

Do not give it its own arrival source: the allotment band (.48) already feeds the block, and a second source is a different brief. Do not draw the glass as a live composite over the whole frame — the ground is a CACHE, so the fixed panes belong in it and only what changes is drawn live. Do not add a second new species 'while you are there'; one is the claim, and two makes the census delta unreadable.

queue.brief: Three faults, one subject: the town names more than it admits to naming, less than it draws, and some things it has deliberately hidden. (a) `cv.style.cursor = live ? 'pointer' : 'default'` keys on `answersTouch(x,y)`, which is the SOWABLE-cell test — so everything #113 opened up (roof birds, windows via `FACES`/`faceAt`, the vanes, the tree crowns) is findable on a desktop only by accident, and the naming and the affordance disagree. The cursor should become a hand wherever the town has a name to give. (b) The roof furniture is not named at all: `drawWashLine`, `drawWaterTank`, `drawPigeonLoft` and `LOFTS[]` put 24 pieces on the near roof — at a phone size the most pointable objects in the frame — and they say nothing, while `livingAt`, `pavingAt` and `FACES` answer for everything else in the town. Give them lines the way #113 gave the birds theirs: off what they ARE, in the town's own words, never a second table of boxes. (c) `nearHidden(y, sy)` is draw-side only — it is called inside `drawBird`/`drawCat`, not in the hit test — so a walker or bird behind the sill is still hit-tested and still named. Make the hit test read the same predicate the renderer does.

Quote it as a table against HEAD, the way #113 did.

queue.brief: The town's ORIGINAL lawn and lane birds are all but extinct, and nobody decided that. Their band's cap is `birds.filter(b => !b.plaza).length < 3`, which counts #106's ROOF birds and the belfry flock against them. #113 measured it over 1551 daylight dry samples across 5 seeds: the gate is open 15.3% of the time and held shut by roof birds alone 84.7% of the time, and mean present is 0.06 lawn/lane against 2.66 roof and 1.31 plaza. The predicate is the bug — the roof band has its own roll and its own `ROOF_BIRDS 3` cap, and the plaza band has `b.plaza`, so the ground band should count only its own members. Fix the membership test, then RE-PRICE rather than leaving the old number in place: 3 was chosen when this was the only band, so measure what 3 actually delivers once it means what it says and set the cap from that.
queue.successLooksLike: Mean lawn/lane birds present in daylight rises from HEAD's 0.06 to a number a wide shot can see, quoted as a presence mean over >= 10 seeds x several days with HEAD as the control — and the roof and plaza means barely move, which is what shows you fixed the count and not the world.
queue.avoid: Do not give the ground birds a new source: the band exists, it is only miscounted. This changes how often the roll is reached, so it reshuffles the seeded world — read the census for COLLAPSE, not delta, and replay any stray motion gate on HEAD before believing it.
